caseno: Appeal From Original Order No. 20 of 1986.
lawyer:
Alimuzzaman Chowdhury with Shamsul Haque Chowdhury and others ----- For the Appellants. 
Sharifuddin Chaklader and others ----- For the Respondents.
parties:
Bangladesh Supreme Court Bar Association, and others ----- Appellants
Vs.
MH Khandkar, Senior Advocate, and others ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
2. The plaintiffs who are nominated members of the Bangladesh Bar Council filed Title Suit No. 923 of 1985 and subsequently prayed for temporary injunction. The case of the plaintiffs in brief, is that they are the nominated members of the Bangladesh Bar Council and they are also the members of the Supreme Court Bar Association which is purely a non-political organisation and the object of the Supreme Court Bar Association is to give all facilities to its members for conducting their legal profession. In the application for temporary injunction it has been stated that the defendant No. 1 has been trying by undue pressure, threat and coercion to fore the plaintiffs to resign from the nominated membership of Bangladesh Bar Council. For that purpose the defendant No. 1 got adopted a number of resolutions which were all held without quorum requiring the plaintiff resign from the membership of the Bangladesh Bar Council. The defendant No. 1 on 1-12-85 in the general meeting got a resolution passed requiring the plaintiff to resign within 3 days from their membership of the Bangladesh Bar Council. Thereafter, within two days the executive committee was requested to issue show cause notice for disciplinary action under article 51 of the Constitution of the Supreme Court Bar Association. The defendant No. 1 thereafter, held a meeting of the executive committee and thereafter, in the, adjourned meeting dated 5-12-85 got a resolution passed requiring the plaintiffs to resin from the membership of the Bangladesh Bar Council. The copy of the said resolution of the executive committee was served on the plaintiffs. That resolution dated 1-12-85 alleged to have been passed by the defendant No. 1 and the subsequent resolutions of the adjourned meeting of the executive committee of the Bangladesh Supreme Court Bar Association held on 5-12-85 was passed in contravention of law and Rules framed under the constitution of the Bangladesh Supreme Court Bar Association. 1980. That in the said injunction petition it has been specifically stated that the plaintiffs will suffer irreparable loss and injury if the illegal resolution No. 1 dated 1-12-85 passed in general meeting and the resolution dated 5-12-85 calling special general meeting fixing 8-1-86 the plaintiffs individual rights to remain as members of the Supreme Court Bar Association will be seriously affected. Further, it has been stated that in the event of passing of any resolution on 8-1-86 as contemplated in the notice will amount to dismembering the Bangladesh Bar Council duly constituted by law and the individual rights of the plaintiffs prayed for a temporary injunction not to hold the alleged meeting on 8-1-86 in pursuance of the show cause notice issued on 8-12-85 upon the plaintiffs. The plaintiffs, further asserted that they have got a good prima facie case and they balance of convenience and inconveniences is in their favour and their right to remain a member of the Bar Association being threatened, they are entitled to the order of temporary injunction. 

 3. The defendant No. 1 Supreme Court Bar Association and defendant No. 2 its Secretary, contested the application for temporary injunction by filing a written objection denying the material allegations made in the application for temporary injunction. The defendant contended that by the resolution dated 1-12-85 and 5-12-85 calling a Special General meeting on 8-1-86 under Article 51 of the Constitution of the Bangladesh Supreme Court Bar Association, 1980, the defendants have merely asked the plaintiffs to show cause as to why disciplinary action should not be taken against them and as such the suit as well as the application for temporary injunction is premature and is liable to be dismissed for want of cause of action. There is no threatened injury of any kind and, as such, the application for temporary injunction is not maintainable under Order XXXIX, Rule 1 and 2 of the Code of Civil procedure. The elected Bar Council was dissolved on the 11th of April, 1982 under MLO 11 of 1982 and thereafter, the bar Council was constituted with the nominated members. That in the General Meeting of the Supreme Court Bar Association held on 15-11-83 the members of the association unanimously passed the resolution requesting the plaintiffs to resign from the membership of the Bar Council, but the plaintiffs having not complied with the request, another General Meeting was held on 15-11-84 and the members of the association in that meeting unanimously reaffirmed the above resolution dated 15-11-83 and once again decided to request the plaintiffs to resign from the Bangladesh Bar Council. That thereafter, the members of the associations by its general meeting dated 6-5-84 requested the executive committee to take disciplinary action against the plaintiffs and further requested the executive committee to issue show cause notice upon the plaintiff and others. That in the general meeting hold on 1-12-85 and in the meeting of the executive committee dated 5-12-85 resolved to serve the plaintiffs with notice to show cause as to why they should not be proceeded against as per provision of Article 51 of the Constitution of the Supreme Court Bar Association for violating the decision of the general meeting and with that end in view the purported Special General Meeting was scheduled to be held on 8-1-86. The defendant further asserted that the plaintiffs have no prima facie case and that the balance of convenience and inconvenience is in favour of the defendants inasmuch as, the defendants will suffer irreparable loss it they are restrained from holding the meeting on 8-1-86. The further case of the defendants is that four nominated members of the Bar Council have already resigned in obedience to the resolution of the Bangladesh Supreme Court Bar Association. The defendants further contended that the petition temporary injunction is misconceived and is liable to be rejected. 

 5. Secondly, he contends that no consequential relief having been sought for in this case the suit is hit by section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. Thirdly, he submits that an application for temporary injunction can be filed subsequently but not simultaneously inasmuch as, in the present case the suit and the application for temporary injunction were filed on tile same date. He next contended that the Supreme Court Bar Association being not a registered Association all the members of the executive committee ought to have been made a party and all the members having not been made parties, the suit is liable to be dismissed and the plaintiffs are not entitled to get temporary injunction in the instant case. 

 6. Mr Muzammel Haque Bhuiyan and Mr. AJ Mohammad Ali, the learned Advocates for the plaintiff respondents submit that the plaintiffs have got a good prima facie case end the balance of convenience and inconvenience is in favour of the plaintiffs and if the prayer for temporary injunction is not granted then the rights of the plaintiffs to remain the members of the Supreme Court Bar Association will be seriously affected and, as such, they have filled the application for temporary injunction in appropriate time considering the threatened action which is proposed to be taken by the Association. Secondly, they summit that the question of mention ability of the suit will be gone into at the time of trial and this issue cannot be decided in this application when prima facie the plaintiffs have got an arguable case, They further contend that in view of the amendment of Order XX, rule 5 of the Code of Civil Procedure, the question of deciding a suit purely on the question of maintainability is no longer available to the appellants. They also submitted that application under Order 1, rule 8 of the Code of Civil Procedure having been filed in the lower court, the question of throwing the suit does not arise on the ground of defect of parties. 

 7. Is this suit the plaintiffs have prayed for a decree declaring that the resolution No. 1 dated 1-12-85 passed in General Meeting on 5-12-85 calling for special General Meeting fixing 8-1-86 and notice of show cause dated 8-12-85 of the Supreme Court Bar Association is illegal, ultra vires, without jurisdiction and not binding upon the plaintiffs and further that the defendants No. 1 and 2 have not legal right to case loss of membership of the plaintiffs under Articles 51 of the Constitution of the Supreme Court Bar Association, 1980. This is the main prayer that was made in the suit. After filing of the Suit this application for temporary injunction was filed and moved on the same day. The plaintiffs were apprehensive of the proposed meeting and in view of that they filed the application for injunction so that the Association cannot hold the purported meeting on 8-1-86. The main question here, is whether the plaintiffs had any cause of action for filing this application for temporary injunction. We find that the plaintiffs have challenged the resolution of the Supreme Court Bar association by saying that the same is illegal, ultra vires, without jurisdiction and void, ab-initio and not done in accordance with the constitution of the Bangladesh Supreme Court Bar Association, 1980, Without going into the question of maintainability of the suit which will be decided by the trial court itself at the appropriate time, it will be worthwhile to see whether the plaintiffs have a prima facie and arguable case and whether their application for injunction is premature and misconceived. 

 8. The plaintiffs have sought for a declaration that what the Association is doing is not in accordance with its constitution and the same is also ultra vires of the constitution of the Supreme Court Bar Association and void and not binding upon the plaintiffs. In such circumstance it cannot be said that the application is premature. Mr. Alimuzzaman Chowdhury has cited the case of the Draper vs British Optical Association, that case we are afraid has no manner of the application in feats of the present case. In that reported decision it has been held that in order to get an injunction the plaintiffs has got to satisfy the Court what the defendant association has done, or is threatening to do, that which is ultra vires and in a proper case the court will determine matters of this kind in a quia timet action. Thus, we find that the plaintiffs in the present cased has been able to show that the defendants are threatening or intending to do what they are not entitled to do under law. 

 9. In the present case, suit was filed on 29-12-83 and on the same day the application for temporary injunction was filed. We do not understand the logic of his argument that an application for temporary injunction can be filed subsequently but not simultaneously. If there is a threatened cause of action and the plaintiffs think that their right to remain members of the Association will be affected adversely by holding a meeting then we do not find any reasons as to why the application for temporary injunction cannot filed be filed. A suit having been filed and thereafter, an application for injunction having been moved the question of seeking consequential relief under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act does not arise. An application for temporary injunction in a suit for such a declaration cannot be a consequential relief as has been urged by the learned Advocate for the appellant. In the case of Mrs. June Ferguson vs Ameenur Rasheed Chowdhury reported in 1973 25 DLR 1 and in the Case of Musammat Rabeya Khatun vs Md. Elias Mollah reported in 28 DLR 181 it has been held that temporary injunction can be given even in a suit for simple declaration without any consequential relief. 

 10. On a consideration of the materials on record, we find that the plaintiffs have been able to make out a prima facie arguable case, and if the temporary injunction is not granted and in the meanwhile the proposed meeting which was scheduled to be held on 8-1-86 take place and the proposed action is taken then the right of the plaintiffs to remain as members of the association will be affected. Thus, we find that the balance of convenience is in favour of the plaintiffs. The plaintiffs are members of the Supreme Court Bar Association and they have challenged the actions of the Executive Committee on the basis of the illegal resolution to hold the proposed meeting and, as such, if the order of temporary injunction be not granted then the plaintiffs will be seriously prejudiced and the very purpose of the suit will be frustrated and the plaintiffs will suffer irreparable loss and injury which cannot be compensated in terms of money. Thus, we find that the learned Sub-ordinate judge has rightly passed the order of temporary injunction in the present case. Further, we find from the impugned order that the learned Sub-ordinate Judge has also directed the parties to take steps for early disposal of the suit where all controversies between the parties will be settled within a short time. Thus, the learned Sub-ordinate Judge has rightly passed the order of injunction on the cardinal principle governing the issuance of injunction and, as such, we do not like to interfere with the impugned order.
